OBSERVED: POST /api/auth/logout accepts client-selected idempotency_key as any non-empty string up to 128 characters.
handleLogout queries prisma.auditLog.findFirst using only requestId=idempotency_key and action in [AUTH_LOGOUT, AUTH_LOGOUT_ALL].
The replay lookup is not bound to authenticated session id, user/email hash, revoke_all mode, or a request fingerprint.

After current-session lookup and device-binding validation, any prior matching audit row causes an immediate 200 {revoked:true} return before checking whether the current session is revoked and before executing the logout mutation.

Therefore a key previously used by a different principal or by the same principal with a different revoke_all payload can short-circuit a later valid logout request without revoking the current requested session set.
SPEC_FACTS: Final DOC-C §4.2 raw paragraphs 10128-10152 define POST /api/auth/logout purpose as revoke current or all sessions.
The route requires session auth and OWNER/OPERATOR/AUDITOR RBAC.
Idempotency is required and retry is safe if the same idempotency key is used.
Request includes optional revoke_all:boolean and required idempotency_key:string.
ENGINEERING_INFERENCE: An idempotent replay may return a stored successful outcome only for the same logical operation identity. An unrelated principal/payload key collision cannot safely stand in for the requested revoke-current/revoke-all mutation.
Because the accepted key domain is client-controlled rather than globally collision-proof, correctness cannot rely on uniqueness by convention.
EXPECTED: Bind logout idempotency identity to the authenticated principal/session and semantic request fingerprint (including revoke_all), or use a dedicated idempotency record that can prove exact replay. A mismatched reuse must not return a false successful revocation.
REPRODUCTION: Have principal A complete a logout using idempotency_key K so an AUTH_LOGOUT/AUTH_LOGOUT_ALL audit row exists with requestId K.
Have a distinct valid principal B submit logout with its own valid CSRF/session/device binding and the same client-valid key K.
Static trace: prior becomes non-null from A's audit row; B's session/device checks pass; the prior branch returns 200 revoked:true before prisma.$transaction revokes B's session.
Equivalent same-principal semantic collision: reuse K with a changed revoke_all value; action-family lookup treats AUTH_LOGOUT and AUTH_LOGOUT_ALL as interchangeable and returns prior success.
